Acute inflammation, characterized by a short-term response, is beneficial and essential for recovery (Medzhitov 20.
However, complications can occur if the inflammatory response persists for a long time or becomes exaggerated.

Chronic inflammation is closely associated with various diseases, such as cardiovascular disease, arthritis, diabetes, and certain types of cancer (Zitvogel et al. In recent years, an increasing number of compounds exhibiting potent antiinflammatory activity have been reported.

Generally, the regulation of pro-inflammatory enzymes is considered one of the most important mechanisms underlying their effects (Rakesh et al. 2015; Rakesh et al. 2017a, b; Chen et al. 2017; Rakesh et al., 2019; Ullas et al. 2020; Verma et al. These pro-inflammatory enzymes include, but are not limited to, cytosolic phospholipase A2 (cPLA, cyclooxygenases (COX), lipoxygenases (LOX), and nitric oxide synthase (NOS) (Li et al. Therefore, developing more effective therapeutic approaches that can precisely control the inflammatory response is necessary to reduce the incidence of chronic diseases and autoimmune disorders.
Consequently, discovering new anti-inflammatory agents from nature is of great importance (Moudgil and Venkatesha 20.

To diversify the chemical spaces of the microbial natural products, we employ a high salt stress strategy to 9H‑carbazole derivatives from a Streptomyces species under potassium iodid cultivate microorganisms (Wang et al. 2007, 2009a, 2009b; Lu et al. 2008; Zheng et al. 2009, 2010; Peng et al. 2011a, 2011b, 20.

In previous research, we applied sodium fluoride (NaF) and sodium bromide (NaBr) to physiologically stress the marine-derived Streptomyces sp. OUCMDZ-5511, resulting in the production of various carbazole alkaloids.

These included 1-chloro-4-methoxy-9H-carbazol-8-ol, known for its anti-quorum sensing activity (Liu et al. 20, and 4-bromo-3-methoxy-9H-carbazole-8-ol, recognized for its anti-inflammatory properties (Yan et al. To continuously activate the silent natural product synthetic gene cluster, we used 7.5% potassium iodide (KI) stress as the salt stress to cultivate the strain OUCMDZ-5511.
As a result, a more active anti-inflammatory iodinated carbazole new derivative (3) was obtained.

Additionally, two other new iodinated carbazole derivatives (1 and 2), a novel oxazolefused chlorinated carbazole derivative (4), and five known analogues (5–9) were also produced by Streptomyces sp. OUCMDZ-5511 under KI stress (Fig. New compounds 3 and 4, as well as the known compounds 6 and 8, exhibited potent anti-inflammatory activity in a zebrafish model.

Actinobacterial strain The actinobacterial strain OUCMDZ-5511 was isolated from Thai mangrove soil and identified as a member of the Streptomyces species based on its 16S rRNA gene sequence and morphological characteristics (Liu et al. 2024; Yan et al. Cultivation and extraction Spores were inoculated into 150 mL of A1 medium, contained in a 500 mL flask.
This medium was prepared by dissolving soluble starch (10 g), yeast extract (4 g), peptone (2 g), and Fe (SO ) ·7H O (0.04 g) in 1 L of distilled 2 4 3 2 water.
The flasks were shaken at 180 rpm and maintained at 28 ℃ for 3 days to prepare the seeding solution.

Subsequently, the seeding solution was distributed into 100 flasks, each containing 100 g of corn, 80 mL of A1 medium, and 7.5 g of KI. Following 30 days of static culture at 28 ℃, the medium from each flask was extracted three times with 600 mL EtOAc (200 mL per extraction) for 24 h. The combined EtOAc solutions were concentrated under vacuum, yielding 13.6 g of extract.

Purification The EtOAc extracts (13.6 g) was divided into nine fractions (Fr1–Fr using a silica gel VLC column with a stepwise gradient elution of petroleum ether (PE) and CH Cl in ratios of 1:0, 10:1, 5:1, 1:1, and 0:1 (v/v), followed by elution with CH Cl /MeOH at ratios of 80:1, 10:1, 1:1, and 0:1 (v/v).
Fr2 (PE/CH Cl , v/v = 10:1, V = 1.5 L, 0.9 g) was further divided into eight subfractions (Fr2.1–Fr2. using a Sephadex LH-20 column with MeOH.

In contrast, iodinated compounds are relatively rare, making them a unique and intriguing area of study (Williams et al. To date, approximately 182 naturally occurring organoiodine compounds have been documented and summarized in the literature (Wang et al. 20, underscoring their scarcity compared to their chlorinated and brominated counterparts.
This rarity underscores the importance of investigating iodinated natural products and their potential biological effects.
One possible explanation for this rarity is the low concentration of iodine in oceanic environments, which is nearly de stress and t… 741 in zebrafish.

Nevertheless, iodinated natural products have been identified across a variety of biological sources, which can be broadly classified into three categories: marine organisms, terrestrial organisms, and abiotic sources.

Among these, marine organisms, particularly algae, sponges, and corals, serve as the primary producers of iodinated compounds (Wang et al. This prevalence in marine ecosystems underscores the ecological significance of these unique compounds despite their limited abundance.

Based on their chemical structures, iodinated natural products from these diverse sources have historically been classified into five main structural types: volatile compounds with short carbon chains, nucleoside derivatives, amino acid derivatives (including those derived from tyrosine, 7 42 tryptophan, and histidine), fatty acid derivatives, and terpenoid derivatives.
These iodinated compounds exhibit a wide range of biological activities, including anticancer (Sonnenschein et al. 20, antifungal (Chan et al. 19, and antibacterial properties.
However, research on the antiinflammatory activity of iodinated compounds remains limited, and reports specifically addressing the oxazole-fused carbazole natural products are even scarcer.
This highlights the need for further investigation into these unique and potentially bioactive molecules.

Interestingly, five novel oxazole[5,4-c]-fused carbazole derivatives were synthesized as early as 1985 (Kansal et al. 19 and 1986 (Sundaramoorthi et al. 19, but their biological activities were not explored at the time.

This study not only successfully obtained the new iodinated natural products (1–3) but also represents the first isolation and identification of a naturally occurring oxazole[5,4-c]-fused carbazole derivative (4).

The migration of immune cells to sites of inflammation is a hallmark of the inflammatory response, which we observed in zebrafish following temporary exposure to CuSO , consistent with previous studies (Zhang et al. However, pre-treatment with compounds 3 and 4 significantly inhibited this migration, as evidenced by the markedly reduced recruitment of immune cells to the damaged lateral line neuromasts, indicating their potent anti-inflammatory effects (Fig. This finding, combined with our previous reports (Yan et al. 20, suggests that the presence of 3-methoxy, 8-hydroxy, and 4-bromo or 4-iodo substitutions are key functional groups contributing to the anti-inflammatory activities of the 9H-carbazoles.

Additionally, 9H-carbazole derivatives 2, 6, and 9, all bearing 3-methoxy and 6-hydroxy substitutions, also demonstrated anti-inflammatory activities (Tables S3 and S. Notably, compound 6, which possesses an additional 4-chloro substitution, exhibited a more potent anti-inflammatory response than the positive control, indomethacin.
This suggests that the presence of 3-methoxy, 6-hydroxy, and 4-chloro groups collectively contributes to the anti-inflammatory properties of the 9H-carbazoles.

Furthermore, the activities of these derivatives decreased in the following order: 4-Cl (6), 4-H (9), and then 4-I (2), indicating that chlorine substitution is more effective than iodine in 9H-carbazoles bearing 3-methoxy and 6-hydroxy groups.

Additionally, when the 3-position is substituted with methoxy, the anti-inflammatory activities of the 6-OH (2, 6, and 9) and 8-OH (3) substitutions were found to be more effective compared to 6-H substitution (1, 5, and 8).

It is well established that CuSO -induced inflammatory reactions are mediated by activation of the Myd88/ NF-κB pathway, leading to the release of pro-inflammatory cytokines (Hu et al. Pre-treatment with compound 3, the most potent compound, effectively suppressed this signaling cascade (Fig. 4A–J) and enhanced the expression of anti-inflammatory mediators, such as PPARγ (Fig. as demonstrated by the normalization of aberrant gene expression profiles.

Therefore, the iodinated new compound, 4-iodo-3-methoxy-9H-carbazole-8-ol (3), is likely to exert its anti-inflammatory effects by modulating the Myd88/ NF-κB signaling pathway, as we previously demonstrated with 4-bromo-3-methoxy-9H-carbazole-8-ol (Yan et al. Together, these compounds represent two promising candidates for the development of novel therapeutic strategies against inflammatory diseases.

In conclusion, this research investigates the biosynthesis potential of 9H-carbazole derivatives from a Streptomyces species subjected to KI stress, leading to the discovery of a variety of halogenated carbazole compounds with promising anti-inflammatory properties.

The study unveiled three new 4-iodocarbazole derivatives (1–3) and one novel 4-chloro oxazole[5,4-c]-fused carbazole derivative (4), which feature an additional oxazole ring, alongside five previously known carbazole derivatives (5–9).

The incorporation of iodine and other halogens into the molecular structures highlights the unique ability of Streptomyces strain OUCMDZ-5511 to utilize halide salts from the cultivation medium to synthesize halogenated carbazole derivatives, thereby expanding the chemical diversity of these compounds.

Additionally, the new iodocarbazole (3) and the novel oxazole-fused chlorocarbazole (4) have demonstrated significant anti-inflammatory activity, underscoring their potential as promising drug candidates for treating inflammatory conditions and paving the way for further exploration of their therapeutic applications.
